entries.test: Compare major technology companies’ public AI claims around 2022 with demonstrated product capabilities and their messaging by June 2024 to assess exaggeration and the shift toward long-term promises.
entries.note: The surrounding text identifies the shift as a move from near-term product claims to long-term promises; the exaggeration alternative does not require proving private intent.

entries.test: Public AI leadership statements, reporting on LLM reliability, and documented business outcomes through June 2024 would show whether messaging shifted toward larger, unverifiable long-term promises as reliability problems became widely known and earlier business promises mostly went unmet.
entries.note: This describes a publicly assessable change in messaging and business results, although some characterizations are evaluative.
The extracted proposition centers on Marcus’s judgment that the extrapolation is wild. He does not endorse Suleyman’s forecast.

entries.test: Amodei’s public statements and reproducible evaluations of Anthropic’s products available by June 2024 would establish whether he promoted those scientific capabilities while the products frequently failed basic reasoning tasks.
entries.note: “Fantasizing” is Marcus’s characterization of public promises; the substantive product-performance assertion is testable.

entries.test: A recording or transcript of Altman’s Aspen remarks and the publicly available supporting evidence at the time would establish what he claimed and whether the claim had evidentiary support.
entries.note: “Without offering” narrows the original assertion of no evidence to what Altman presented. Marcus endorses the criticism, not the quoted GDP possibility.
